purpose: Teach: 付着/印鑑/コンペ/足場/自粛/増減/連覇/鉄人

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 創業時、本気で、絶対、製品に、絶対、ゴミ、付着、絶対、避けるよう、絶対、徹底したぞ、お父さん、本気で、頼んだぞ、絶対、本気、本気で、絶対。
lines.en: In the early days, we were absolutely serious about keeping any contamination off our products. I drilled it into you, and I'm counting on you to carry that forward with the same commitment.
lines.style: Measured, slightly fading voice. Pauses between thoughts like memory is retrieving each piece. Quiet pride beneath the instruction. Lean toward firmness only on the repeated absolutes—not for emphasis but for weight.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_boss
lines.jp: はい。お父さんの代から、本気で、絶対、印鑑、絶対、こだわって、絶対、守ってまいります、本気で、感謝
lines.en: Yes. Since your generation, I've studied those principles carefully—the product standards, the quality marks—and I'm keeping that foundation exactly as you taught it. I'm truly grateful.
lines.style: Formal deference with underlying warmth. Measured cadence, each clause deliberate. Soft landing on the gratitude—not performative, genuine acknowledgment. The posture of a son speaking to his father's memory.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 創業期、本気で、絶対、業界コンペ、絶対、連戦連勝、お父さん、本気で、頑張ったぞ、お前にも、本気で、頼んだぞ、絶対、本気、絶対、本気で。
lines.en: In those early years, we competed in industry championships constantly—and we won, every time. Your father worked with everything he had. I'm asking you to inherit that same spirit.
lines.style: Voice carries the weight of those victories. Slightly slower on the memories. Leans into the competitive pride without boasting. The final ask softens—becomes almost intimate, like a relay baton being passed.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_boss
lines.jp: はい。お父さんの代から、本気で、絶対、当社の足場、絶対、しっかり、固められてきました、本気で、感謝
lines.en: Yes. I've studied the ups and downs of our business during your father's era very carefully. I've learned from every decision he made. Thank you for that foundation.
lines.style: Steady, formal register. Each sentence sits fully before moving to the next. Gratitude lands softly but with real weight. The studied part is quieter—it's not boasting, it's homework done with care.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 創業期、本気で、絶対、社員の自粛、絶対、お父さん、徹底させたぞ、お前にも、本気で、絶対、引き継いで欲しい、絶対、本気、本気で、絶対。
lines.en: In the founding era, I insisted on discipline from the staff—real discipline. I made sure everyone understood what mattered. I'm asking you to carry that forward too.
lines.style: Voice hardens slightly on 'discipline' and 'understood'—not angry, but firm in the way an elder lays down expectation. Quieter on the final ask. The repetition of 'I'm asking' becomes almost tender despite the steel.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_boss
lines.jp: はい。お父さんの代の、業績の増減、本気で、絶対、私、絶対、勉強してきました、本気で、感謝
lines.en: Yes. I've studied the company's performance through all your father's years—the rises and the falls—and I've learned the lessons behind each. I'm truly grateful for what he built.
lines.style: Thoughtful, slightly slower pace. The studying part is sincere—he's done the work. Lands on gratitude with quiet conviction. No rush. The voice carries both humility and the weight of responsibility understood.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 業界、本気で、絶対、連覇、絶対、お父さんの代、何度も、絶対、達成したぞ、お前にも、本気で、頼んだぞ
lines.en: Our industry championships—we won consecutively, year after year, in those early days. Your father achieved that repeatedly. I'm asking you to live up to that legacy.
lines.style: Voice opens with quiet pride on the championships. Each victory gets its own moment. The final ask drops in register and tempo—becomes almost vulnerable. Like he's handing over something irreplaceable.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_boss
lines.jp: はい。お父さん、本気で、絶対、鉄人並みの、絶対、経営者でしたよね、本気で、感謝、しております
lines.en: Yes. Your father was truly an extraordinary executive—an iron will in human form. I'm grateful for everything he was and everything he left us.
lines.style: Gentle, reflective close. Not eulogy—something warmer and more immediate. The 'iron will' phrase lands with quiet admiration, not hyperbole. Final words slow slightly, allowing the gratitude to settle. Posture of a son at peace with inheritance.
